h: Helping Nervous First-Timers Find Their Feet
p: Not every child bounds onto an obstacle course full of confidence. Some hang back, watch the others and need a bit of time before they'll try. That's completely fine. A good approach is to start with the lower, simpler obstacles and celebrate small wins, like making it halfway along a balance section or holding on for a few extra seconds.

If you're joining in as a parent, going first and falling off cheerfully is one of the best things you can do. It shows them that coming off is part of the game, not a failure, and the big padded landings make it far less scary than it looks.

Leicester has plenty of family-friendly extras to fill the rest of the day. Abbey Park, just north of the centre, has riverside paths, play spaces and the remains of Leicester Abbey. Leicester Market is a great place to grab some food, and the city's famous Golden Mile on Belgrave Road is known for its Indian restaurants and sweet shops. Out of town, Bradgate Park offers wild-feeling countryside with herds of deer roaming freely, and Twycross Zoo is within a sensible drive for a separate day out.
Whatever you pick, do the session first while everyone has the most energy, then let the rest of the day unfold more slowly.
